publicReleaseNotes: Uptime 0.5.1 fixes sign-in for an owner who has enrolled a second factor: the console now asks for it instead of showing Access denied, at the address the owner opened, with an authenticator code, a recovery code or a passkey, and the Lobby, sign-in pages and alert drill links reach the same step. A member who is not the owner and has enrolled a factor still verifies each new sign-in with the command line. The route editor on a monitor now sets teams, environment, severity, check-location and origin filters, and daily or business-hours quiet hours, and its check panel can drill a route; Settings › Alerts manages teams and each person's opt-in. Alert routing is still partly built: expiry and renewal notices do not follow routes. An owner or administrator can export a chosen set of up to 100 monitors through the archive API, with no console control yet. Icon-only controls show tooltips, interrupted incident-comment mention emails are sent once by the next scheduled run, and recurring maintenance across a daylight-saving change is proven. Agents can delete an internal incident comment under the company's policy. Two additive migrations (0084 and 0085), no new required settings, and @runeditrun/rer is pinned to exactly 0.2.96. Back up before upgrading; monitors, history, incidents, destinations and private settings are kept. Known issue: a response body over 64 KiB still fails the check, so monitor a smaller page such as a health endpoint. The product screenshot was taken on 0.4.0, before the console changes of 0.5.0 and 0.5.1. Product screenshot: .github/assets/release/uptime-0.4.0-monitor-1440.png
